title: Sales/CS Request Crystallizer: bundle + rapid-scope for large accounts
creator: Leah Mendoza
description: Problem: Sales and CS receive high-volume, often overlapping enterprise feature asks. Manual triage is slow, inconsistent, and produces uneven scopes for the same account or cohort. This causes long sales cycles and missed opportunities for bundling cross-account asks into roadmaps. Goal: Build a repeatable, semi-automated 'Crystallizer' process that aggregates Sales/CS feature requests, deduplicates and bundles by account/cohort, produces a concise rapid-scope envelope, and assigns a recommended prioritization bucket for PM review within 48-72 hours.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Intake form + data capture exists and is adopted by Sales/CS for >= 80% of tracked enterprise asks.
A2: Aggregation pipeline produces consolidated bundles per account/cohort and flags duplicates with >= 85% precision on a 100-sample test.
A3: Each bundle includes: 1-line summary, 3-line use case, impact score (0-10), suggested release surface (hosted/dedicated/private), and 2-point engineering estimate OR urgency note.
A4: First-pass scoping time (from intake submission to PM-ready bundle) averages <= 48 hours for high-priority accounts and <= 72 hours overall.
A5: PMs can approve/adjust bundle and trigger a follow-up (discovery/POC) from the Crystallizer UI or playbook.
proposed_solution: MVP approach: 1) Standardize intake: single Sales/CS form (Google Form or internal Airtable) with structured fields (account, use case, expected volume, security constraints, add-on vs core). 2) Automated aggregator: nightly job that ingests new entries, normalizes text, maps to account records, groups similar asks using TF-IDF + fuzzy matching, and outputs candidate bundles. 3) Scoring rubric: compute a short value-feasibility-risk score using heuristics (customer size, revenue proxy, implementation complexity, compliance needs). 4) Rapid-scope template: generated bundle with suggested next step (quick win, scoped feature, enterprise program) and a 1-2 point dev estimate. 5) Hand-off: PM review queue in internal Console; PM either approves for discovery or returns to CS with clarifying questions. Deliverables: intake template, aggregation script, scoring rubric, Crystallizer playbook, and a lightweight PM review dashboard.
notes: Stakeholders: Growth/Revenue Ops (submitters), Solutions Engineering (technical validation), Legal/Compliance (if flagged), Eng triage/Platform PMs.
MVP scope excludes full engineering design; focus is on first-pass normalization + recommendation only.
Trade-offs: automated grouping risks over-merging distinct asks — include manual override and per-item provenance in outputs.
Risk: data quality from Sales notes; mitigation: required structured fields and one mandatory customer quote/example.
Alternative considered: fully manual weekly intake reviews (rejected due to slow turnaround).
